name: Strong Technical Candidate
description: Thorough, structured explanation with exact syntax and concrete examples

turns.speaker: agent
turns.text: Let us start with worksheets and workbooks. Can you explain the difference?

turns.speaker: candidate
turns.text: A workbook is the entire Excel file, like sales_2026.xlsx. Inside it you have individual sheet tabs like January and February. You can right-click a sheet tab to rename it or drag it to reorder.

turns.speaker: agent
turns.text: How do cells and references work when copying formulas?

turns.speaker: candidate
turns.text: A cell is addressed by column letter and row number, like B3. When I write =A2 and copy it down one row, it becomes =A3 because it is a relative reference. But $A$1 is an absolute reference where dollar signs lock both column and row so it does not change when copied.

turns.speaker: agent
turns.text: How do formulas and functions work?

turns.speaker: candidate
turns.text: Every formula starts with an equals sign. =SUM(A1:A10) adds the numbers in that range. For logic, =IF(B2>=50,"Pass","Fail") tests a condition. I also use AVERAGE for means and COUNT for numbers.

turns.speaker: agent
turns.text: Tell me about formatting, tables, and charts.

turns.speaker: candidate
turns.text: Number formats change appearance: 0.1 becomes 10% under percent format, and currency adds ₹ or $. In tables, header rows let you sort all rows together or filter to hide non-matching rows. For charts, I select data like A1:B5 and add a clear chart title and label axes.
